account.disabledNoIssue: The account "{account}" is disabled, so nothing is issued on its behalf.
account.nobodyCalled: There is nobody called "{name}" in this realm's directory. In product mode every referenced object must exist first.
account.realmRetiring: The trust realm "{realm}" is being removed, so nothing new is signed in or issued in it.
account.realmRetiringInterrupted: The trust realm "{realm}" was being removed from {since}, and that removal was interrupted before it finished — the process doing it stopped. Nothing new is signed in or issued in it until an administrator finishes the removal.
account.realmRetiringSince: The trust realm "{realm}" is being removed (the removal began at {since}), so nothing new is signed in or issued in it.
authn.accountNoLongerSignedIn: That account is no longer signed in here. Choose it again to sign in, or choose another.
authn.accountNotRemembered: That account is not one this browser remembers.
authn.accountSessionEnded: That account's session has just ended. Choose it again to sign in, or choose another.
authn.accountStillSignedIn: That account is still signed in. Sign it out first; only a signed-out account can be forgotten.
authn.accountsChanged: The accounts in this browser changed in another tab. Choose again.
authn.accountsFull: This browser is already signed in to {count} accounts, the most it may hold. Sign out of one of them first.
authn.accountsUnread: This browser's accounts could not be read just now. Try again in a moment.
authn.afterStepGone: This step after signing in has expired or does not exist. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.apiBadLimit: The limit {limit} is not a string or a list of strings of a reasonable size.
authn.apiCsrf: The {header} header is missing or is not this browser's. Load the sign-in page again.
authn.apiFailed: Something went wrong; this sign-in could not continue.
authn.apiJsonOnly: This operation takes a JSON body (Content-Type: application/json).
authn.apiNoAccountChoice: There is no sign-in waiting on an account choice under that id, or it has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.apiNoSession: This browser holds no session for this sign-in. Load the sign-in page again.
authn.apiNoSignIn: There is no sign-in waiting under that id, or it has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.apiNotAStepPage: That is not a page of a sign-in step.
authn.apiNotConsentId: That is not the id of a consent.
authn.apiNotPasswordChangeId: That is not the id of a password change.
authn.apiNotSignInId: That is not the id of a sign-in.
authn.apiOrigin: This operation is sent by a page of this service: the request carried {origin, select, other {another origin} none {no Origin}}.
authn.apiOtherBrowser: That sign-in was started in another browser.
authn.apiSessionCap: This realm is holding as many sign-in sessions as it allows, so no new one can start in this browser now. Try again later.
authn.apiUnknownField: The body has a field this operation does not take: {field}.
authn.applicationNoPasskey: This application does not allow a passkey sign-in.
authn.authenticatorAppNotSetUp: The authenticator app could not be set up.
authn.authenticatorAppsOff: Authenticator apps cannot be set up in this realm.
authn.browserAnswerUnreadable: The browser returned something this server could not read.
authn.browserNoCeremonySignIn: Your browser did not run the ceremony. Signing in with a passkey needs JavaScript — a passkey is used by the browser and no form can do it. Allow scripts for this page, or type your username.
authn.browserNoCeremonyStep: Your browser did not run the ceremony. This step needs JavaScript — a passkey is used by the browser and no form can do it. Allow scripts for this page and try again.
authn.browserNoPasskey: Your browser did not use a passkey ({error}).
authn.certificateNone: No verified client certificate arrived on this connection, so there is nobody to continue as. Choose the certificate when your browser asks, or sign in another way.
authn.certificateNotAPerson: This certificate is not a TLS client certificate for a person here, so it cannot sign you in.
authn.certificateNotOffered: Signing in with a certificate is not offered for this sign-in.
authn.certificateNotStored: Your certificate is not stored on any account here, so it cannot sign you in. Ask an administrator to store it on your account (a renewed certificate is stored again), or sign in another way.
authn.certificateOfApplication: This certificate was issued to an application, and an application's certificate signs nobody in.
authn.certificateOtherRealm: Your certificate was issued in another realm, so it cannot sign you in here.
authn.certificateRevoked: Your certificate has been revoked, or its revocation could not be confirmed, so it cannot sign you in.
authn.certificateStoredTwice: Your certificate is stored on more than one account here, so it cannot say which one is yours. Ask an administrator to store it on yours alone.
authn.certificateUnavailable: Signing in with a certificate is not available here.
authn.choosePasskeyFirst: Choose one of your passkeys first.
authn.chooseSecondFactorFirst: Choose a second factor to set up first.
authn.codeUncheckedTryAgain: That code could not be checked. Try again.
authn.codeUncheckedTryNext: That code could not be checked. Try the next one.
authn.emailAnswersNeither: This sign-in asks for a security key or a password, and an emailed {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} answers neither.
authn.emailAskNewLink: Ask for a new one on the page where you started signing in.
authn.emailCodeExpired: That code has expired. Send a new one.
authn.emailLinkNotLatest: That link is not the latest one sent. Use the newest message.
authn.emailNoCodeYet: No code has been sent for this sign-in yet.
authn.emailNoMoreSends: No more {kind, select, code {codes} other {links}} can be sent for this sign-in. Start again from the application that sent you here.
authn.emailNoStep: There is no sign-in waiting for an emailed {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} here. It may have finished, or run out of time.
authn.emailNotOffered: This realm does not offer an emailed {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} as a way to sign in.
authn.emailNotSent: The message could not be sent just now.
authn.emailOtherBrowser: This link works only in the browser where you started signing in.
authn.emailOtherBrowserCopy: This link works only in the browser where you started signing in. Copy it into that browser, or start again here.
authn.emailTooSoon: One was sent less than {seconds} seconds ago. Check your mail, or wait a moment and ask again.
authn.emailUnchecked: That {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} could not be checked just now.
authn.emailUsed: That {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} has already been used.
authn.emailWrong: That {kind, select, code {code} other {link}} is not right. {left} more attempt(s) before this sign-in ends.
authn.enterUsername: Enter a username. It does not have to exist — it is the identity the issued tokens will describe.
authn.hardwarePasskeyNone: This sign-in asks for a hardware-protected phishing-resistant passkey, and none of the passkeys held for this step can earn it. A synced passkey, or one whose attestation is not trusted, is not enough.
authn.keyAloneAccountNeedsTwo: A second factor is required for this account, and a security key on its own is one factor. Sign in with your password; you will be asked for your second factor, or to set one up.
authn.keyAloneRealmNeedsTwo: A second factor is required in this realm, and a security key on its own is one factor. Sign in with your password; you will be asked for your second factor, or to set one up.
authn.keyDemanded: This sign-in demands a passkey, and {what, select, recovery {a recovery code} other {a one-time code}} does not answer that. Use your passkey on the previous screen.
authn.linkNeedsPassword: Linking an account signs in with its password — and its second factor, where it has one — so a security key on its own is not offered here.
authn.linkNoPasskeyAlone: Linking an account signs in with its password, so a passkey on its own is not offered here.
authn.newPasswordNotAccepted: The new password was not accepted.
authn.noAuthenticatorApp: No authenticator app is enrolled for that account, so there is no code to ask for.
authn.noClassicalPasskeyLeft: There is no classical passkey to upgrade any more.
authn.noPasskeyRegistered: There is no passkey registered for signing in to this account. Sign in with your password, then add a passkey at /portal/keys.
authn.noPasswordStep: There is no sign-in waiting for a password as its second factor. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.noRecoveryCodes: No recovery codes have been issued for that account, so there is nothing to ask for.
authn.noSecondFactorPasskey: No passkey is registered as a second factor for that account.
authn.passkeyAloneNotTwo: This request asked for a second factor, so a passkey on its own cannot answer it — one factor is one factor. Sign in with a password and the passkey together.
authn.passkeyBeforeUsernameless: This passkey was registered before passkeys could sign in without a username. Type your username to use it, or register it again at /portal/keys.
authn.passkeyCouldNotSignIn: That passkey could not sign you in.
authn.passkeyNameNotUsername: That is the name your password manager shows for a post-quantum passkey, not a username. Type your username without the part after the "+".
authn.passkeyNeededNoneHeld: This request needs a passkey, and this account holds none. Add one at /portal/keys and sign in again.
authn.passkeyNotRecorded: The passkey could not be recorded. Try again.
authn.passkeyNotUpgradable: The passkey could not be upgraded.
authn.passkeyRequestExpired: That passkey request has expired. Try again.
authn.passkeyRulesUnchecked: This passkey could not be checked against this realm's rules. Try again.
authn.passkeyUncheckedUnchanged: The passkey could not be checked. Your passkey is unchanged; try again.
authn.passkeysOffNoRegistration: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled), so a new one cannot be registered here. A passkey already registered goes on working.
authn.passwordNotFirstFactor: This realm does not accept a password as a first factor. Use one of the other ways of signing in below.
authn.passwordReserved: That password is reserved and is refused at every sign-in, so it cannot be yours.
authn.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords are not the same.
authn.policyRefusedSession: The issuance policy refused this session.
authn.postLoginNotSkippable: The time allowed for this has passed, so it cannot be skipped any more. Register the passkey to finish signing in.
authn.postLoginOtherActivityPasskey: This step asks for another post-login activity, not a passkey.
authn.postLoginOtherActivityMail: This step asks for another post-login activity, not a mail encryption key.
authn.postLoginOtherActivityPiv: This step asks for another post-login activity, not a PIV certificate.
authn.postLoginPivSlotsOpen: Enrol a new certificate for slot(s) {slots} first.
authn.postLoginOverdueHere: Before you can sign in this way you have to register a post-quantum passkey, and the time allowed for it has passed. Sign in at this service's sign-in screen, where you will be asked to register it.
authn.postLoginStepHeld: You have to complete a step after signing in. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.postQuantumOnlyStep: This step registers a post-quantum passkey only; a classical one cannot be made here.
authn.productNoPrimaryKey: This service is in product mode, where a passkey that signs in on its own is added at /portal/keys after signing in, never at the sign-in screen.
authn.productNoSuchPerson: This service is in product mode, where a passkey can only be registered for somebody who already exists. Create the person first.
authn.recoveryCodesSpent: Every recovery code on that account has been used. A set is issued once and is never topped up, so an administrator has to clear it before a new one can be issued.
authn.roleExclusive: At most one of these roles may be chosen together.
authn.roleLapsed: A role chosen is no longer available. Choose again.
authn.roleNotChoosableHere: This application needs you to choose a role when you sign in, which cannot be done this way. Sign in at this service's sign-in screen.
authn.roleNotOffered: A role was chosen that this sign-in did not offer.
authn.roleRequiredLeftOut: This sign-in needs at least one of its required roles.
authn.rolesAfterSignIn: You have to choose your roles after signing in. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.rpIdMismatch: webauthn.rpId is "{rpId}", which is neither the host this request reached ("{host}") nor a registrable domain suffix of it, and in product mode a security-key ceremony is not run against an address the configuration did not name. Reach this service at a host under "{rpId}", or set global.publicBaseUrl to one.
authn.secondFactorAlreadySetUp: A second factor is already set up for this account. Start the request again from the application that sent you here and sign in with it.
authn.secondFactorCheckFailed: The second factor did not verify; this check failed: {checks}.
authn.secondFactorDemandUnmet: This sign-in needs a second factor that this application does not accept, or one you have not set up. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNoneAvailable: A second factor is needed and none that this realm accepts is available for this account.
authn.secondFactorNoneForApplication: A second factor is required, and none that this application accepts can be set up here. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNoneInRealm: A second factor is required for this account and none can be set up here: authenticator apps and security keys are both switched off in this realm. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNoneToEnrol: This application accepts a second factor you have not set up, and none that it accepts can be set up here. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNotOptional: A second factor is required for this account; it cannot be ignored.
authn.secondFactorUnchecked: The second factor could not be checked: {detail}
authn.secondFactorUncheckedAgain: The second factor could not be checked. Try again.
authn.securityKeysOff: Security keys cannot be set up in this realm.
authn.setUpExpired: That set-up expired before it was confirmed. Start it again.
authn.setUpGone: This second-factor set-up has expired or does not exist. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.stepEnded: This sign-in step has already ended. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.stepExpired: This second-factor step has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait {seconds} seconds and try again.
authn.tooManyFailedAttempts: Too many failed attempts. Wait {seconds} seconds and try again.
authn.upgradeExpired: This passkey upgrade has expired. Start over to sign in again; you will be asked again.
authn.usernamelessOnly: This application signs in with a passkey and no username. Use Sign in with a passkey.
authn.walletOtherPerson: The credential your wallet presented was issued to somebody other than the person whose password was entered, so neither is signed in.
authn.walletStepExpired: This second-factor step has expired. Start the request again from the application.
authn.walletTwice: The first factor of this sign-in was already a wallet, and one key proved twice is one factor. Use your authenticator app, your passkey or your password.
authn.webauthnError: {error} (WebAuthn reports one error for several situations, so this does not say which.)
consent.formExpired: This consent form has expired, or it has already been answered. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
consent.limitsOnlyLowered: The limits of "{type}" may only be lowered here: {raised}.
consent.nobodySignedIn: Nobody is signed in here any more, so there is nobody to record an answer for. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
consent.nobodySignedInAnswer: Nobody is signed in here any more, so this answer belongs to nobody. Nothing was recorded.
consent.nothingWaiting: There is no consent waiting under that id, or it has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here — nothing was issued and nothing was recorded.
consent.otherPerson: This consent was asked of "{asked}" and the session in this browser belongs to "{signedIn}". It is refused rather than recorded against whoever happens to be signed in, which is the one failure at this door that would write something untrue into the directory.
consent.otherPersonAnswer: This consent was asked of "{asked}" and this browser is signed in as "{signedIn}". Nothing was recorded.
consent.receiversUnticked: Every receiver of "{type}" was unticked; untick the right itself to leave it out.
description.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
description.unknownView: The service sent a view this page does not know ({kind}).
did.authorizationNotStored: the directory did not store the authorization.
did.changeSignedBy: a change of {did} is authorized by the DID itself, signing with a key its current version ({version}) names; this answer was signed by {signer}.
did.deactivated: that DID is deactivated; a deactivated DID takes no change.
did.historyFull: {did} has {versions} versions, the most one DID keeps; publish a new DID and deactivate this one.
did.keyAlreadyCurrent: that key is already in the current version of {did}; prove a new one.
did.keyNotProved: the key of {did} was handed to you and has not been proved with a wallet; prove it (Enrol a wallet, signing as the DID) before changing it.
did.keyNotSealed: the new private key could not be sealed, so the DID was not changed.
did.newKeyUnauthorized: a new key is accepted only after a key {did} names now authorized the change, in the last {seconds} seconds.
did.noSuchDid: you have no published DID with that id.
did.notAnAct: that is not a DID act.
did.publishingOff: this realm does not publish DIDs for people (did.personPublishing is off).
did.realmGeneratesKey: this realm generates the key of a DID it publishes; publish one from the portal.
did.realmHoldsKey: the key of {did} is held by this realm; change it with its own Add key or Rotate key.
did.versionNotStored: the directory did not store the new version.
did.walletKeyChange: the key of {did} is held by your wallet, so a change is authorized by a key it names now and proved by the new key: two wallet round trips, started from its Add key or Rotate key.
factor.backupMismatch: That is not one of your recovery codes.
factor.backupNoneFor: No recovery codes have been issued for {name}.
factor.backupShape: A recovery code is letters and digits only — the ones this service printed for you, in groups. Dashes and spaces are ignored.
factor.backupSpent: That recovery code has already been used. Each one works once — use the next unused code on your list.
factor.backupUnreadable: Your recovery codes cannot be read by this service, so they cannot be checked. An administrator has to clear them on your row under /admin/users.
factor.backupUnrecorded: That code is right and this service could not record that it has been used, so it was not accepted. Try another one, and tell an administrator.
factor.codeUncheckedAgain: That code could not be checked just now. Try again in a moment.
factor.codeUncheckedNext: That code could not be checked just now. Try the next one in a moment.
factor.hotpMismatch: That code is not right. If your token has been pressed many times without signing in, resynchronise it with two codes in a row.
factor.hotpNoneFor: No one-time code token is enrolled for {name}.
factor.hotpReplay: That code has already been used. Press your token again for a new one.
factor.hotpResyncMismatch: Those two codes are not consecutive codes of this token within {window} presses. Press it twice more and enter both codes.
factor.hotpResyncShape: Resynchronising takes two codes of {digits} digits, one after the other.
factor.hotpUnreadable: Your one-time code token cannot be read by this service, so it cannot be checked. An administrator has to clear it.
factor.hotpUnreadableShort: Your one-time code token cannot be read by this service.
factor.nameControlCharacter: The name holds a control character, so no person has it. Nothing was started.
factor.secretUnreadable: The stored shared secret could not be read.
factor.totpEnrolExpired: That enrolment has expired. Start again and scan the new code.
factor.totpMismatch: That code is not right, or it has expired.
factor.totpNoName: There is no name to enrol an authenticator for.
factor.totpNoStore: No credential store is installed, so an authenticator app cannot be enrolled.
factor.totpNoneFor: No authenticator app is enrolled for {name}.
factor.totpOff: Authenticator apps are turned off on this service (the authentication policy).
factor.totpReplay: That code has already been used. Wait for your authenticator to show the next one.
factor.totpUnreadable: Your authenticator enrolment cannot be read by this service, so it cannot be checked. An administrator has to clear it on your row under /admin/users and you can enrol again.
factor.yubiNoneFor: No YubiKey OTP is enrolled for {name}.
factor.yubiNotDecrypted: That OTP does not decrypt under the key enrolled here.
factor.yubiOtherKey: That OTP was not made by the YubiKey enrolled here.
factor.yubiReplay: That one-time password has already been used. Touch the key again.
factor.yubiShape: That is not a YubiKey OTP. Touch the key and enter the whole string it types.
factor.yubiUnchecked: That one-time password could not be checked just now. Touch the key again in a moment.
factor.yubiUnreadable: Your YubiKey OTP cannot be read by this service, so it cannot be checked. An administrator has to clear it.
factor.yubiZeroCounter: That OTP carries a zero counter, which this service does not accept. Touch the key again.
federation.attributePolicyMissing: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this realm's attribute policy requires {missing} of every person and the partner supplied no value of it, so nobody was created. Map the attribute on the relationship (fedAttributeMap), or provision the person first.
federation.attributeSourceRefused: {why} This realm's attribute source says a sign-in it cannot read is refused, and the session was ended.
federation.consumerProvidersOff: This relationship is a consumer or social provider, and this realm has federation.consumerProviders off.
federation.disabled: It exists and is configured, and fedEnabled is FALSE. Every relationship is created disabled deliberately: a partner that half-exists and silently accepts assertions is the failure this whole register is arranged to prevent. Enable it on /admin/federation.
federation.fapiNeedsDiscovery: fedFapi is {profile} and fedDiscovery is off. The pushed authorization request endpoint is read from that document, so the sign-in is not started.
federation.formIncomplete: The form was sent {attempts} times without the values this service needs, so nothing was created. Start the sign-in again.
federation.formNoToken: The form did not carry the token this step was given, so nothing was created. Start the sign-in again.
federation.initiateLoginOff: fedInitiateLogin is off on "{id}", so a sign-in its partner starts (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4) is refused. Turn it on to accept one; until then a person signs in from this service.
federation.issuerNotPeer: The request names the issuer "{iss}", and this relationship is with "{peer}". OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4 makes iss REQUIRED, and it is how this service knows which partner started the sign-in.
federation.linkNeedsSignIn: This step needs a sign-in here as {username}, made through the linking screen just now, and this browser holds {held, select, none {none} other {a different one}}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.linkOtherBrowser: This linking step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.linkSignInEnded: Linking your account at the partner to {username} needs you to sign in here as {username} first, and that sign-in ended without one ({asked}). Nothing was linked and nothing was written.
federation.linkSubjectChanged: While you were signing in, the partner's subject came to name {named} rather than {username}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.linkSubjectChangedSomebody: While you were signing in, the partner's subject came to name somebody else rather than {username}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.noAccountCreated: The assertion verified, and this service will not create an account from it.
federation.noEntryAutocreateOff: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this service holds no directory entry for {username}, and dynamic provisioning (fedAutocreateUsers) is off on this relationship, so the person has to be created here first — through SCIM, /admin/users/new or the management API — and linked to the partner's subject.
federation.noEntryNotCreated: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this service holds no directory entry for {username}, and the directory would not create one (the subject policy refused it, the relationship's fedProvisionCap is full, or the directory is full).
federation.noIssuer: The request names no issuer, and this relationship is with "{peer}". OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4 makes iss REQUIRED, and it is how this service knows which partner started the sign-in.
federation.noLinkWaiting: The linking step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.noParEndpoint: fedFapi is {profile} and the discovery document names no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint.
federation.noRelationship: There is no relationship called {id}. The configured ones are on the federation index.
federation.noSessionStarted: The assertion verified, and this service will not start a session from it.
federation.noStep: The step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the sign-in again.
federation.noStepFederated: The step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.notAnIdentifier: Type an address such as user@example.com, or a URL.
federation.notConfigured: It is enabled, but {missing} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} still empty. It refuses rather than half-working — a federated sign-in that got half way and produced a session would be the worst possible outcome.
federation.notFoundByWebFinger: fedWebFinger and fedDiscovery must both be on, and the relationship enabled and fully configured, before an identifier is looked up for it.
federation.off: federation.enabled is off, so no federation endpoint answers. No relationship was changed.
federation.otherWay: "{id}" is an identity-provider-side relationship: this service ASSERTS to that partner rather than consuming from it. There is nothing to sign in to here. A partner this service both consumes from and asserts to is two relationships — see federation/CLAUDE.md.
federation.policyRefusedSession: The assertion verified and the partner is configured — this service will not start a session for {username} because the issuance policy said no. That is a POLICY decision rather than a problem with the assertion or with the partner, so retrying will not change it. The role an application requires is on /admin/roles and the document that decides is on /admin/xacml.
federation.providerNotThisPartner: WebFinger named the issuer "{issuer}", which does not begin with this relationship's fedPeer "{peer}". Only an issuer within the partner an administrator configured is used.
federation.recordedOnAfter: , and every refusal is also a row in the audit log.
federation.recordedOnBefore: This is recorded on the relationship as fedLastError. The whole record is at
federation.refusesHere: This service refuses rather than accepting here, which is the opposite of what it does everywhere else. What arrives at a federation endpoint is an unauthenticated request claiming to be a person, and the session it would produce is the one every other protocol in this process reads. See federation/CLAUDE.md.
federation.relationshipGonePartner: The relationship "{id}" is disabled, half-configured or gone since the partner answered.
federation.relationshipGoneProvider: The relationship "{id}" is disabled, half-configured or gone since the provider answered.
federation.requestNotMade: The request could not be made.
federation.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
federation.ssfSignsNobodyIn: "{id}" is an ssf relationship: the partner sends this service Shared Signals, and signs nobody in.
federation.stepOtherBrowser: This step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Start the sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.stepOtherBrowserFederated: This step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Start the federated sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.stepUpNeedsFactor: This sign-in needed a second factor held here, as {username}, made just now, and this browser holds {held, select, none {none} other {a different authentication}}. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.unknownView: The service sent a view this page does not know ({kind}).
federation.webFingerNoIssuer: WebFinger at {host} named no OpenID Connect issuer.

federation.what.failedLookingUp: This service failed while looking the identifier up
federation.what.failedStarting: This service failed while starting the sign-in
federation.what.fapiNeedsDiscovery: This FAPI profile needs the partner's discovery document
federation.what.fapiNotSigned: The FAPI request could not be signed
federation.what.mayNotStart: That partner may not start a sign-in here
federation.what.noParEndpoint: The partner publishes no pushed authorization request endpoint
federation.what.noProviderFound: No OpenID Provider was found for that identifier
federation.what.notAnIdentifier: That is not an identifier WebFinger can look up
federation.what.notConfigured: That relationship is not fully configured
federation.what.notFoundByWebFinger: That partner is not found by WebFinger here
federation.what.notProvisioned: This person has not been provisioned

gnap.limitsNotAccepted: These limits could not be accepted: {why}
gnap.linkNotActive: The link does not belong to a request that is still waiting for approval — it may have expired, been used already, or been answered.
gnap.linkOnce: Each interaction link works once (RFC 9635 section 4).
gnap.noSession: This browser holds no session for this page. Load the page again.
gnap.notWaiting: There is no request waiting for approval at this address, or it was already answered or has expired.
gnap.notYours: It asks for access to a resource that is not yours to give: {why} Only its owner can approve it.
gnap.nothingApproved: Nothing was approved and nothing was sent to any application. Start again from the application that sent you here.
gnap.off: This trust realm does not run GNAP (gnap.enabled).
gnap.requestNotCompleted: The request could not be completed.
gnap.tooManyCodes: Too many codes have been tried from here. {detail}

limits.tooManyActs: You have done that too many times in a short while. Wait {seconds} seconds and try again.
logout.accountNotSignedIn: That account is not signed in in this browser any more. Choose again.
logout.accountsOff: This trust realm does not keep several signed-in accounts per browser (authn.multipleAccounts is off), so there is no account to choose.
logout.chooseAccount: Choose an account, or every account.
logout.familyUnreadable: This could not be read: {failure}. Everything else on this page is unaffected, and a global logout still tries this family again.
logout.nameRefusedAnyUserOff: logout.anyUser is off on this instance, so /logout acts only on the session you are holding. It was asked about "{asked}". To sign another person out, use /admin/logout (the console's Admin Write role) or POST /admin-api/logout (an access token carrying admin:write).
logout.nameRefusedProduct: This service is in product mode, where a sign-out cannot name somebody else whatever logout.anyUser says, so /logout acts only on the session you are holding. It was asked about "{asked}". To sign another person out, use /admin/logout (the console's Admin Write role) or POST /admin-api/logout (an access token carrying admin:write).
logout.noSessionClosed: There is no session cookie on this request, and naming somebody is closed ({closed, select, anyUser {logout.anyUser is off} other {product mode}}), so there is nobody for this endpoint to act on. Sign in at /authn/login first.
logout.noSessionOpen: There is no session cookie on this request. Name somebody with ?username=, or sign in at /authn/login first.
logout.nobodyToSignOutClosed: There is nobody to sign out: this request carries no session cookie, and naming somebody is closed ({closed, select, anyUser {logout.anyUser is off} other {product mode}}).
logout.nobodyToSignOutOpen: There is nobody to sign out: this request carries no session cookie and named no username. A POST is never redirected to the sign-in screen — a 303 would make it a GET and the fields would be gone.
logout.nothingTicked: Nothing is ticked, so nothing was ended.
logout.postedNoOrigin: This page is posted by the sign-out page of this service: the request carried no origin of this service.
logout.postedOtherOrigin: This page is posted by the sign-out page of this service: the request carried another origin.
logout.refusedDevelopment: Sign in as that person at /authn/login — no password is checked in development mode /admin/logout is the operator's door and is behind the console's two roles.
logout.refusedVerifies: Signing yourself out needs no role; signing somebody else out is an act on their account and needs the operator's door. /admin/logout is the operator's door and is behind the console's two roles.
logout.resultExpired: That sign-out result has expired. What is still live is at /logout.
logout.resultNone: There is no sign-out result here.
logout.resultNotOne: That is not a sign-out result.
logout.resultNotOurs: That sign-out result was not made by this service.
logout.resultOtherRealm: That sign-out result was made in another trust realm.
logout.resultUnreadable: That sign-out result could not be read.
logout.row.claimsTokenEnded: that persisted claims token had already ended
logout.row.codeRedeemed: that authorization code has already been redeemed or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.row.credentialForgotten: that credential is no longer in the issued register — it has been forgotten to the cap since this list was drawn, at which point this service has no position on it left to state
logout.row.gnapGrantFinalized: that GNAP grant had already been finalized
logout.row.gnapGrantGone: that GNAP grant has already been revoked or finalized
logout.row.grantGone: that grant has already been revoked or has expired
logout.row.grantRevoked: that grant has already been revoked
logout.row.noSession: there was no session {handle} to end; it had already expired or already been signed out
logout.row.partnerHsm: the partner cannot be told: its sign-out is signed by a key in the HSM, and it was not signed ahead of this sign-out
logout.row.partnerSessionEnded: the session that partner signed in has already ended
logout.row.preAuthorizedRedeemed: that pre-authorized code has already been redeemed or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.row.realmSessionEnded: the session that realm was signed into on has already ended, which took its cleanup list with it
logout.row.rpSessionEnded: the session that relying party was signed into on has already ended, which signed it out too
logout.row.spSessionEnded: the session that service provider was signed into on has already ended, which took its logout list with it
logout.row.walletCredentialDisowned: that wallet credential has already been disowned or has expired
logout.row.walletSignInCollected: that wallet sign-in has already been collected or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.signInAgain: Sign in again, then come back to end your other sessions.
logout.signInAgainFirst: Sign in again at /authn/login, then come back to end your other sessions.
logout.unreachable: The service could not be reached, so nothing was signed out. Check the connection and try again.
passkey.alreadyEnrolled: That authenticator is already enrolled. Use a DIFFERENT one — a backup on the same device is lost with the original.
passkey.assertionAnswered: this sign-in step has already been answered
passkey.assertionNothingToSpend: The assertion names no credential or challenge, so it cannot be spent.
passkey.assertionUnchecked: the assertion could not be checked just now
passkey.attestationAlgorithm: {at, select, registration {That passkey's attestation } other {This passkey was registered with an attestation that }}{state, select, untrusted {{at, select, registration {is not one this service verified and trusts} other {this service did not verify and trust}}} nocert {carries no certificate} unrecorded {is signed with algorithms never recorded} other {is signed with {signed}}}, and this realm requires one signed with {anyRequired, select, no {nothing} other {{required}}} (the passkey policy's attestationAlgorithms). {at, select, registration {Use an authenticator whose attestation is signed that way.} other {Sign in another way, and register a passkey whose attestation is.}}
passkey.backupEligible: That passkey can be synced or backed up (its authenticator set the backup-eligible flag), and this realm accepts only device-bound passkeys (the passkey policy's backupEligibility is disallow). {at, select, registration {Use a security key, or a passkey kept on this device only.} other {Sign in another way, and register a device-bound key.}}
passkey.counterBehind: the signature counter did not increase (now {now}, highest seen {highest}) — the key may have been cloned
passkey.counterUnchecked: the signature counter could not be checked just now
passkey.credProtect: That passkey protects its credential at level {level}{note, select, unattested { (its attestation is not trusted, so the level it reported is not proof, and counts as level 1)} unreported { (it reported no credential protection, which is level 1)} other {}}, and this realm requires level {required} (the passkey policy's credProtect, enforced). Use a security key that supports CTAP 2.1 credential protection.
passkey.enrolmentOff: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled). A passkey already registered goes on being listed; no new one can be registered.
passkey.enrolmentUseless: This realm accepts a passkey neither as a way to sign in on its own nor as a second factor (webauthn.primaryAllowed, webauthn.mfaAllowed and the authentication policy), so a new one could never be used.
passkey.importCredProtect: This person's passkey policy enforces CTAP 2.1 credential protection (credProtect level {level}), and an imported U2F key cannot prove its level. Register a security key instead.
passkey.issuancePolicy: This realm's issuance policy {at, select, registration {does not let that passkey be registered here.} other {no longer lets that passkey sign you in. Sign in another way.}}
passkey.justRegistered: That authenticator has just been registered by another request. It is enrolled once; look for it on your key list.
passkey.laneClassicalOnly: The passkey policy offers classical passkeys only here (registrationMode is classical-only), so a post-quantum one cannot be created. A post-quantum passkey already registered goes on working.
passkey.laneNoMlDsa: This service can verify no ML-DSA algorithm, so a post-quantum passkey cannot be created.
passkey.laneNotAlongside: A post-quantum passkey beside a classical one is not offered in this realm (webauthn.pqcAlongsideClassical{pqcOnly, select, yes {, and webauthn.pqcOnly is on} other {}}). A post-quantum passkey already registered goes on working.
passkey.notALane: A passkey is created in the "classical" lane or the "pqc" lane. "{lane}" is neither.
passkey.notPrimary: A passkey cannot sign anybody in on its own in this realm (webauthn.primaryAllowed). Sign in with a password, and your passkey is asked for next where the realm allows it.
passkey.notRegisteredNow: The security key could not be registered just now. Try again.
passkey.notSecondFactor: A passkey cannot be a second factor in this realm (webauthn.mfaAllowed). An authenticator app is the other one, where the authentication policy allows it.
passkey.off: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled).
passkey.pinLengthShort: That passkey accepts a PIN of {value} characters, and this realm requires at least {min} (the passkey policy's minPinLength). {at, select, registration {Use a key configured with a longer minimum PIN.} other {Sign in another way, and register a key whose minimum PIN is long enough.}}
passkey.pinLengthUnreported: That passkey did not report its minimum PIN length, and this realm requires a PIN of at least {min} characters (the passkey policy's enforcePinLength). A security key reports it only to services it was configured to tell. {at, select, registration {Use a key configured with a longer minimum PIN.} other {Sign in another way, and register a key whose minimum PIN is long enough.}}
passkey.postQuantum: That passkey signs with {known, select, no {a classical algorithm} other {{algorithm}}}, and this realm requires a post-quantum passkey, one that signs with ML-DSA (the passkey policy's postQuantumRequired is {setting}). {at, select, registration {Use an authenticator that can make an ML-DSA passkey.} other {Sign in another way, and register a post-quantum passkey.}}
passkey.profileAlgorithm: That passkey signs with {known, select, no {an algorithm never recorded} other {{algorithm}}}, which is not one the passkey policy offers here (profile {profile}: {anyOffered, select, no {nothing} other {{offered}}}, registrationMode {mode}). Use an authenticator that can make one of those.
passkey.recoveryEnrolFirst: This account was recovered without its passkey, and this realm lets it reach no application until a passkey has signed you in (the passkey policy's recoveryAssurance). Register a new passkey, then sign in with it.
passkey.recoverySelfService: This account is protected by a passkey, and this realm lets it be recovered only by whoever manages it (the passkey policy's recoveryAssurance is operator-only). Sign in with your passkey, or ask an administrator for a reset or activation link.
passkey.retryPqOnlyProfile: The passkey policy offers post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkeys only here (registrationMode is pq-only), so a classical one cannot be made instead. Use a device or a security key that can make an ML-DSA passkey.
passkey.retryPqcOnly: This realm requests post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkeys only (webauthn.pqcOnly), so a classical one cannot be made instead. Use a device or a security key that can make an ML-DSA passkey.
passkey.retryRequiredRegistration: The passkey policy requires a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey at registration (postQuantumRequired is registration-and-sign-in), so a classical one cannot be made instead. Use a device or a security key that can make an ML-DSA passkey.
passkey.retryRequiredSignIn: The passkey policy requires a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey to sign in here (postQuantumRequired), so a classical one made now would not sign you in. Use a device or a security key that can make an ML-DSA passkey.
passkey.serialMissing: That security key's attestation names no device serial this service can read, and this realm binds security keys to the serials issued to each person (the passkey policy's enterpriseSerialAttribute). Use a key from your organisation, registered where enterprise attestation is enabled.
passkey.serialNotHeld: That security key (serial {serial}) is not one issued to you: its serial is not on your directory entry ({attribute}). Use the key your organisation issued you.
passkey.u2fNotAccepted: That security key was imported from a U2F service this realm no longer accepts (webauthn.u2fAppIds).
passkey.u2fNotAlone: That security key was imported from a U2F service and cannot verify who you are, so it cannot sign you in on its own. Use it after your password.
passkey.upgradeAlreadyPq: That passkey is already post-quantum ({algorithm}); there is nothing to upgrade.
passkey.upgradeAtCap: You already hold {count} passkey(s), the most this realm allows, and the upgrade adds one beside this passkey. Remove one first.
passkey.upgradeDone: That passkey was already upgraded: its post-quantum passkey is beside it. Remove that one first to upgrade again.
passkey.upgradeDuplicate: That authenticator is already enrolled. Your passkey is unchanged.
passkey.upgradeGone: The passkey you were upgrading was removed or upgraded by another request since you used it, so nothing was changed.
passkey.upgradeNoMlDsa: This service can verify no ML-DSA algorithm, so a passkey cannot be upgraded to one.
passkey.upgradeNoStore: No credential store is installed, so no passkey can be upgraded.
passkey.upgradeNotInProgress: That passkey upgrade is not the one in progress, or it has expired. Your passkey is unchanged; start again.
passkey.upgradeNotTheirs: No passkey of that id is registered for {name}.
passkey.upgradeNotVerified: The post-quantum passkey did not verify — {checks}. Your passkey is unchanged.
passkey.upgradeOff: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled), so none can be upgraded.
passkey.upgradeProofDone: This passkey has already been used for this upgrade; create the post-quantum passkey now.
passkey.upgradeProofFirst: Use your passkey first, to show it is yours, before the post-quantum passkey is created.
passkey.upgradeUnchecked: The registration could not be checked: {detail}. Your passkey is unchanged.
passkey.usernamelessNotPrimary: A passkey may not sign anybody in on its own in this realm (webauthn.primaryAllowed).
passkey.usernamelessOff: Signing in with a passkey and no username is switched off in this realm (the passkey policy's allowUsernameless, on Directory → Policies).
password.breached: That password has appeared in a data breach, so people trying stolen passwords will try it. Choose a different one.
password.breachedAtSignIn: The password you signed in with has appeared in a data breach, so it has to be changed now. Choose one you have not used anywhere else.
password.missing: Give a password. To take one away, remove the {attribute} attribute from the entry.
password.policy: That password does not meet this realm's password policy, which asks for {short, select, yes {at least {min} characters (it has {length})} other {}}{both, select, yes {, } other {}}{hasWord, select, yes {no word this organization or service is known by (it contains "{word}")} other {}}. The rules are on /admin/policies (profile "{profile}").
password.reused: That password has been used for this account recently. This realm's password policy refuses the current password and the {history} before it (profile "{profile}"). Choose one you have not used here.
password.rotates: {account} is a service account whose password rotates through its push destination, so it cannot be set by hand: the destination is where its consumers read it. Use Rotate now on its page, or POST /admin-api/users/rotate-password.
policy.compliantDeviceRequired: A compliant registered device is required.
policy.deviceBoundPending: The application requires a device-bound session, and registration for this one has not finished.
policy.deviceBoundRefused: The application requires a device-bound session, and this one {fact, select, skipped {was skipped.} other {was not bound in time.}}
policy.indeterminate: the issuance policy could not be evaluated{anyStatus, select, yes {: {status}} other {}}. Nothing is issued on an Indeterminate, because the alternative is issuing on an error.
policy.mechanismRequired: This application requires signing in with {mechanisms}.
policy.noIssuanceDecision: No issuance decision could be made.
policy.otherRuleDenied: the issuance policy denied it with a rule other than the role requirement: "{application}" requires {required}, which {named, select, yes {"{who}"} other {the caller}} holds. {anyCarried, select, yes {The Deny carried {carried}.} other {The Deny carried no obligation naming the rule; /admin/xacml/decide shows which rule applies.}}
policy.passkeyNotFirstFactor: This realm's authentication policy does not accept a passkey as a first factor. Sign in with what it does accept.
policy.passkeyNotFirstFactorShort: This realm's authentication policy does not accept a passkey as a first factor.
policy.passkeyNotSecondFactor: This realm's authentication policy does not accept a passkey as a second factor.
policy.phishingResistance: "{application}" requires {lacked, select, hardware-protected {a phishing-resistant authentication with a hardware-protected key (OpenID Connect EAP ACR Values 1.0, phrh)} other {a phishing-resistant authentication (OpenID Connect EAP ACR Values 1.0, phr)}}, and {named, select, yes {"{who}"} other {the caller}}'s was not one. A passkey or security key already registered meets phr; phrh needs one whose attestation this realm trusts and that is not backup-eligible.
policy.protocolNotConfigured: The application is not configured for this protocol.
policy.roleRequired: "{application}" requires {anyRequired, select, yes {{required}} other {a role nothing named}} and {named, select, yes {"{who}"} other {the caller}} holds {anyHeld, select, yes {{held}} other {no role at all}}.
policy.secondFactorRequired: This application requires the second factor {factors}.
spnego.off: This service can sign people in with a Kerberos ticket, and {setting} is set to false.
spnego.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
wallet.alreadyUsed: This sign-in has already been used.
wallet.anotherIssuer: The credential verified against a certificate in oid4vp.trustedIssuerCertificates, not against this realm's own key. A credential another issuer signed may be presented to this Verifier, and it does not sign anybody in here: only a credential this realm issued can say who a person here is.
wallet.answerWrongOrigin: A wallet's answer is accepted only from the page on {origin} that asked for it.
wallet.cannotSignRequest: This service cannot sign a wallet request at the moment ({reason}). Sign in another way.
wallet.credentialMismatch: The credential does not match what this realm recorded when it issued it (its subject or the key it is bound to), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.dcApiEmpty: Nothing came back from the browser's Digital Credentials API. Use the same-device link instead.
wallet.declined: The wallet declined to present a credential ({error}), so nobody was signed in.
wallet.didActNeedsEnrolment: A DID act is an enrolment's, started from the portal of the person signed in here.
wallet.didRealmKey: The self-issued ID Token names {subject}, a DID this realm published with a key it keeps, which signs nobody in.
wallet.didUnproved: The self-issued ID Token names {subject}, a DID this realm published with a key it handed over and nobody has proved with a wallet; prove it on your portal's Self-issued IDs page first.
wallet.disownedReinstate: This credential has been disowned: {reason}. It still verifies, and it signs nobody in here any more — its status list says so too. An administrator of this service may reinstate it.
wallet.disownedReissue: This credential has been disowned: {reason}. It still verifies, and it signs nobody in here any more — its status list says so too. A credential issued to you after that will: get one issued again on the Wallet page of your account.
wallet.enrolNeedsSession: A self-issued key is enrolled for the person who is signed in, from their own portal, and this browser holds no sign-on session.
wallet.enrolSignedOut: You are no longer signed in as the person this enrolment was for.
wallet.entryGone: The directory entry this credential was issued for no longer exists — it was deleted, or its name now belongs to a different entry — so the credential signs nobody in.
wallet.heading.alreadyUsed: This sign-in has already been used
wallet.heading.answerNotFromPage: That answer did not come from this page
wallet.heading.cannotMakeRequest: A wallet request could not be made
wallet.heading.didActNotStarted: That DID act cannot be started
wallet.heading.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting for this sign-in
wallet.heading.otherBrowser: This sign-in was started in another browser
wallet.heading.policyRefused: The issuance policy refused this sign-in
wallet.heading.responseCodeNotThis: That response code is not this sign-in's
wallet.heading.signInBeforeEnrolling: Sign in before enrolling a wallet
wallet.heading.signInOff: Signing in with a wallet is off
wallet.heading.walletNotRegistered: That wallet address is not registered
wallet.idTokenNotVerified: The self-issued ID Token did not verify, so it signs nobody in. The checks above say which rule it broke.
wallet.keyForSeveralPeople: This wallet key was issued credentials for more than one person here, and an ldp_vc presentation does not say which credential it came from, so it signs nobody in.
wallet.mdocKeyMismatch: The mdoc does not match the device key this realm recorded when it issued it, so it signs nobody in.
wallet.neverStarted: This sign-in was never started here, or it has expired. Each lives oid4vp.signInTtlS seconds.
wallet.notCompleted: The sign-in could not be completed.
wallet.notFinishedTryShortly: This sign-in could not be finished just now; try again shortly.
wallet.notIssuedHere: This realm has no record of issuing this credential to a person it authenticated. Only a credential this realm's issuer minted on an access token this realm issued and verified — for a person, for credential issuance, and not disowned since — may sign somebody in. A credential from another realm, one issued on a token this service did not issue, or one issued before a restart in development mode is not one.
wallet.notOneHolder: The self-issued ID Token and the presentation did not both verify for one holder, so nobody was signed in.
wallet.nothingWaiting: A wallet sign-in continues a request that is waiting at the sign-in screen, and this link names none — it was never started, it has expired, or it has been used.
wallet.otherBrowser: A wallet sign-in finishes only in the browser that started it. If that was you, go back to that browser; otherwise somebody sent you a link to their own sign-in.
wallet.policyRefusedVerified: Your presentation verified. This service will not start a session for this identity. That is a policy decision rather than anything wrong with the credential.
wallet.presentationNotVerified: The presentation did not verify, so it signs nobody in. The checks above say which rule it broke.
wallet.requestExpired: The request you were signing in for has expired. Start again from the application.
wallet.responseCodeMismatch: The link your wallet sent you back with does not carry the code this service gave it.
wallet.selfIssuedNotSecondFactor: A self-issued ID is not offered as a second factor.
wallet.signInOff: This service can sign people in with a verifiable presentation, and oid4vp.signIn is set to false. Turn it on at /admin/oid4vp, or with POST /admin-api/config/set. The Verifier still checks the presentations a verification asks for (POST /admin-api/verifications/start); it signs nobody in.
wallet.signInWithdrawn: This sign-in was ended before this browser collected it: a sign-out. Nobody was signed in.
wallet.signInWithdrawnBecause: This sign-in was ended before this browser collected it: {why}. Nobody was signed in.
wallet.statusNotGood: The credential's status says it is no longer good ({detail}), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.statusRevokedOrSuspended: The credential's status says it is no longer good (revoked or suspended), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.subjectNotEnrolled: The self-issued ID Token verified, and its subject {subject} is not enrolled for anybody here. A self-issued key signs in only the person who enrolled it — sign in another way and enrol it on your portal's Self-issued IDs page.
wallet.verdict.selfIssuedNotVerified: The self-issued ID Token did not verify.
wallet.walletUrlNotListed: The wallet URL "{url}" is neither oid4vp.walletUrl nor one listed in oid4vp.allowedWalletUrls, and this realm does not send a presentation request to an address the request named. Add it to that setting, or leave the wallet parameter off.
web.answeredNoJson: The service answered {status} with no JSON.
web.noOperation: This control has no API operation ({control}), so the page refuses it rather than guess.
web.noState: The service sent no state for it.
web.noStepToRestart: This page names no sign-in step to start over from.
web.notDrawnTitle: This page could not be drawn
web.startAgainFromApplication: Start again from the application that sent you here.
web.unreachable: The service's API could not be reached.
